Granit Xhaka was central to their early set-piece pressure, delivering several dangerous corners that tested the Chelsea backline. The deadlock was finally broken in the 25th minute when Trai Hume connected with a cross from Luke O’Nien following a key pass by Robin Roefs . Hume showed exceptional technique to volley the ball home with his right foot, leaving the keeper with no chance and giving the Black Cats a deserved lead. Second Half Chaos and Palmer’s Response The second half exploded into life shortly after the restart. In the 50th minute, disaster struck for the Blues when Malo Gusto inadvertently turned the ball into his own net, doubling Sunderland 's advantage. However, Chelsea responded almost immediately. In the 56th minute, Pedro Neto found Cole Palmer outside the box; the star forward unleashed a precise left-footed strike to pull one back and ignite hopes of a comeback, making it 2-1. Red Card and a Frantic Finish Just as momentum seemed to shift, Chelsea suffered a significant blow in the 62nd minute. Wesley Fofana , who had been booked only minutes earlier, received a second yellow card and was sent off. Despite being down to ten men, Chelsea pushed forward, introducing fresh legs like Liam Delap . The final minutes were marred by a flurry of yellow cards for players such as Enzo Fernandez , Joao Pedro , and Cole Palmer as tensions boiled over. Ultimately, Sunderland held firm in front of 47,155 fans to secure the victory in a match defined by its physical edge and late-game drama.

In a high-energy preseason encounter, Real Madrid and Athletic Club faced off in a match that provided plenty of attacking flair and tactical intrigue. The contest, held on July 24, 2026 , saw both managers utilize their squads extensively in a clash defined by clinical finishing. Early Pressure and Breakthrough Real Madrid established their dominance early, controlling 74% of the possession throughout the match. The deadlock was broken in the 12th minute when Gonzalo Garcia found the back of the net with a precise right-footed strike, set up by a clever ball from Daniel Carvajal . The opening stages were not without tension, as Thiago Pitarch and Jude Bellingham both found themselves in the referee's book following early challenges. As the first half drew to a close, the game burst into life. In the 41st minute, Jude Bellingham doubled the lead for the hosts with a stunning left-footed volley after receiving a cross from Thiago Pitarch . However, Athletic Club responded almost immediately. In stoppage time, Inaki Williams turned provider for Gorka Guruzeta , who clinicaly volleyed home to reduce the deficit just before the halftime whistle. Second Half Dominance and VAR Drama The second half saw the introduction of fresh legs and a continued offensive push from Real Madrid . In the 51st minute, Kylian Mbappé extended the lead with a powerful effort from outside the box, assisted by Alvaro Carreras . Despite having several goals ruled out for offside, the French forward remained a constant threat to the Athletic Club backline. The drama intensified in the closing minutes. At the 88th minute, Brahim Díaz scored following a VAR review that overturned an initial decision, with Thiago Pitarch claiming another assist. Although Athletic Club managed a late consolation through an Urko Izeta header in the 91st minute—once again assisted by Inaki Williams — Real Madrid held firm to secure a 4-2 victory in an entertaining summer showcase.
